facts.fact: Small businesses typically allocate 5-10% of revenue to marketing, according to the page.
facts.quote: most only allocate **5-10%** of revenue to their marketing

facts.fact: The page states global ad spend is projected to hit $1.17 trillion by 2025.
facts.quote: global ad spend is projected to hit **$1.17 trillion** by 2025

facts.fact: The page states traditional TV production costs historically averaged $250,000 for a national spot in the 2000s.
facts.quote: traditional TV production costs historically hitting an average of **$250,000** for a national spot back in the 2000s

facts.fact: An example goal given is increasing in-store foot traffic by 15% over four weeks.
facts.quote: "**increase in-store foot traffic by 15%** over the next four weeks"

facts.fact: An example goal given is generating 200 new leads through a website contact form in a quarter.
facts.quote: generate **200 new leads** through our website's contact form this quarter

facts.fact: Example objective for a local restaurant: increase weekday reservations by 25% while promoting a lunch special.
facts.quote: increase weekday reservations by **25%**

facts.fact: Example objective for a home services company: generate 50 qualified phone calls for roof inspections before storm season.
facts.quote: Generate **50** qualified phone calls for roof inspections before storm season hits.

facts.fact: Example objective for an e-commerce brand: a 10% conversion rate from viewers who visit the site.
facts.quote: hit a **10% conversion rate** from viewers who visit the site

facts.fact: The page recommends a 30-second spot using a hook in the first 0-5 seconds, solution in 5-25 seconds, and call-to-action in 25-30 seconds.
facts.quote: **The Hook (0-5 seconds):** Open with a relatable problem

facts.fact: The page states that Adwave lets businesses get on TV for as little as $30 per day (vendor's own claim).
facts.quote: Today, Adwave lets businesses get in the game for as little as **$30/day**.

facts.fact: The page cites a projection that the U.S. advertising market will hit $422 billion in 2025 (source not named on the page).
facts.quote: the U.S. advertising market is projected to hit **$422 billion** in 2025

facts.fact: The page states that traditional TV accounts for $50 billion of the U.S. advertising market (source not named on the page).
facts.quote: traditional TV still accounts for a massive **$50 billion** chunk of that.

facts.fact: The page states that a decade ago a 30-second TV spot could easily cost $100,000 to $350,000 to produce or run.
facts.quote: A decade ago, a 30-second spot could easily run you **$100,000 to $350,000**.

facts.fact: The page states that Adwave ads can run across more than 100 premium networks and streaming services (vendor's own claim).
facts.quote: Your ad can run across more than **100 premium networks** and streaming services

facts.fact: The page states the standard TV ad video resolution is 1920x1080 Full HD with a 16:9 aspect ratio.
facts.quote: The standard is almost always **1920x1080** Full HD with a **16:9** aspect ratio.

facts.fact: The page states that in North America the typical TV ad frame rate is 29.97 frames per second.
facts.quote: In North America, this is typically **29.97 frames per second** (fps).

facts.fact: The page states that TV ad audio is typically mixed to a loudness level such as -24 LKFS.
facts.quote: Your ad's audio needs to be mixed to a specific loudness level (like -24 LKFS)

facts.fact: Hiring a local professional crew to produce a TV commercial can cost anywhere from a few thousand dollars to well over $10,000, according to the page.
facts.quote: hiring a local professional crew could run you anywhere from a few thousand dollars to well over **$10,000**.

facts.fact: The standard TV commercial ad lengths listed by the page are 15, 30, and 60 seconds.
facts.quote: The standard ad lengths you’ll see on TV are **15, 30, and 60 seconds**.

facts.fact: The page describes the 30-second spot as the gold standard for most small and local businesses.
facts.quote: For most small and local businesses, the **30-second spot** is the gold standard.

facts.fact: The page states that Adwave's platform automatically schedules ad placements so spend never exceeds the total budget the user sets.
facts.quote: You just set your total budget, and the system intelligently schedules your ad placements to get the most mileage out of every dollar, without ever going over your limit.

facts.fact: Adwave's dashboard, per the page, tracks impressions, reach (unique households), frequency (average times a household saw the ad), and viewer demographics.
facts.quote: **Impressions:** The total number of times your commercial was shown on screen.

facts.fact: The page defines frequency as the average number of times a single household saw the ad.
facts.quote: **Frequency:** The average number of times a single household saw your ad.

facts.fact: The page defines reach as how many unique households have seen the ad.
facts.quote: **Reach:** How many unique households have seen your ad.
